title: Elastic Fairness Gate: proportional admission, outage reconciliation, and multi-region load-shedding
creator: Ava Nguyen
description:
Problem summary: Our current token-based limiter struggles during coordinated client bursts and during regional limiter outages. We observe either unfairness (some tenants exhaust tokens while others are starved) or dangerous fail-open behavior when the limiter control plane loses connectivity. This ticket implements the Elastic Fairness Gate (EFG): a runtime admission layer that enforces proportional admission across tenants during bursts, gracefully reconciles limiter state after outages, and integrates with multi-region failover/circuit-breaker policies to preserve SLOs.

Goals:
- Maintain regional 99th token latency and availability SLOs by preventing tail amplification caused by uncoordinated bursts and limiter rehydration storms.
- Ensure proportional fairness across tenant weights while allowing controlled, short-lived priority overrides for critical customers.
- Provide deterministic degraded behavior when central quota service is unreachable: local soft credits, bounded emergency shedding, and safe downstream signaling (429 with retry-after and structured debug headers).
- Make behavior observable and controllable via runtime flags and console rollouts (canary -> global).

Non-goals:
- This is not a wholesale replacement for centralized quota arbitration; EFG operates as a regional enforcement/coordination shim that cooperates with central leases and cross-region overflow routing.

Key design ideas (short):
1) Proportional Admission Window: per-tenant admission budgets scaled to configured weights rather than fixed tokens. During detected bursts, the gate switches from per-request token checks to a windowed proportional admission algorithm that enforces each tenant's share of available headroom.
2) Stateful Outage Reconciliation: when central quota backplane is unavailable, instances issue short-term local leases (soft credits) with conservative defaults and record immutable reconciliation logs. On full recovery, a deterministic rehydration protocol drains the reconciliation log to avoid stampeding the central service.
3) Bounded Emergency Shedding: a circuit breaker monitors regional SLO proxies (latency p99, queue depth, GPU utilization). When thresholds cross, EFG enacts graduated shedding policies: thrift shed -> proportional soft-shed -> hard quotas, with telemetry-backed automated rollback.
4) Cross-region overflow policy: integrate with smart routing so tenant traffic can overflow to another region where the same EFG policy enforces fairness and prevents overload cascades.

Why now: recent incidents (2026-01-17 and 2026-02-12) showed limiter rehydration storms after control-plane failover causing regional SLO degradation and prolonged customer impact. This ticket addresses the systemic coordination gaps.
acceptance_criteria: EFG implemented behind feature flag and togglable per-region in runtime-2.4 branch
Automated unit + integration tests that simulate: single-region burst, multi-region overflow, central backplane outage, and rehydration storm scenarios
Benchmarked: under synthetic burst (10x baseline RPS for 30s), p99 latency increase < 1.5x and no tenant starved for > 5s (weighted fairness metric within 2% of configured share)
Reconciliation protocol prevents > 10% extra token consumption on recoveries in chaos tests
Console controls for canary rollout and telemetry panels exist (slo, admitted_rate_by_tenant, shed_events, reconciliation_queue_length)
Runbook updated and post-deploy chaos playbook added to oncall docs

Implement rehydration reconciliation log with backoff drains

progress_updates: 2026-02-28 - Ticket created by Ava Nguyen. Initial incident summary and high-level design sketched. Assigned to Rafael Ortiz.

2026-03-02 - Architecture meeting: agreed on local soft-lease model (default TTL=9s) and deterministic reconciliation log format. Tradeoff: shorter TTL reduces risk of double-spend but increases central load on reconnect; chose 9s conservative default after perf sims.

2026-03-04 - Prototype proportional admission implemented in a branch. Initial microbench showed proportional fairness within 1.8% under synthetic weighted clients. Observed small GC jitter at 4k tenants; added pool reuse to allocator plan.

2026-03-06 - Design review with PM and SRE. PM asked for explicit canary abort thresholds; SRE requested additional metrics (reconciliation_queue_length, local_lease_hits). Agreed to add canary abort if p99 latency > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.

2026-03-08 - Integration test harness extended to simulate central backplane outage and multi-region overflow. Discovered a race where multiple instances attempt to drain reconciliation simultaneously; added leader-election by short monotonic epoch token to serialize drain operations.

2026-03-10 - Security reviewed reconciliation logs format. We will persist only non-sensitive keys (tenant_id hashed with SHA256, delta counts) and encrypt with KMS. Security accepted with minor logging redaction changes.

2026-03-12 - PR opened for runtime changes and unit tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3245. Draft console dashboard at https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc/rate-limiter-slo (internal).
2026-03-13 - Canary plan finalized: 5% of regional traffic for 2 hours -> 25% for 6 hours -> 100% if no regressions. Monitoring alerts and canary abort thresholds configured in console.
comments: PM (Jordan Patel) 2026-03-03: Need to show effect on committed customers; add a path for emergency priority override for 3 enterprise accounts.
SRE (Elena Marquez) 2026-03-05: Strong +1 on bounded shedding. Please add metrics for per-tenant rejection rate and mean-time-to-recover after rehydration.
Design (Kai Tan) 2026-03-07: Consider simplifying the reconciliation log format to avoid schema evolution headaches; recommend a v1 append-only file with checksum.
Security (Priya Shah) 2026-03-10: Redact PII from logs and use KMS envelope encryption. Confirmed offline ingestion pipeline will also respect redaction.
Reviewer (Samantha Liu) 2026-03-12: PR looks good; request more integration tests for region-to-region overflow path (simulate increased RTT).
Assignee (Rafael Ortiz) 2026-03-13: Noted. Adding high-latency overflow test and a post-canary chaos run with limiter process restarts.
notes: Rollout considerations: tie canary to customers with low criticality first, use traffic split by tenant hash to ensure predictable bucket shares.
Performance knobs: admission window size and local-lease TTL can be tuned per-region using console; defaults chosen to be conservative.
Testing: use chaos infra to kill central backplane and restart limiter processes in canary region to validate rehydration safety.
